title: Copilot agent draft publish: chain the review request through a GitHub App token, because GITHUB_TOKEN-created events never start another workflow
answers: Why does Copilot review never start after the Copilot agent marks its PR ready for review?
How do I make a workflow's action trigger a different workflow's ready_for_review run?
Where is the Copilot draft PR published to ready for review?
body:
Path: .github/workflows/copilot-agent.yml:publish-draft. This job runs on pull_request_target review_requested events for draft PRs opened by the Copilot bot, mints an app token with actions/create-github-app-token, and runs `gh pr ready`. The ready_for_review event it emits is what starts .github/workflows/copilot-review.yml.
Rule: Events created with the default GITHUB_TOKEN do not start other workflow runs. A step whose side effect must trigger a downstream workflow has to authenticate with the app token (client-id from APP_CLIENT_ID, private-key from APP_PRIVATE_KEY) and pass its output as GH_TOKEN. The publish step in copilot-agent.yml:publish-draft is the reference pattern.
Symptom: The PR was published to ready for review, but Copilot Review never ran, because the ready_for_review event created with GITHUB_TOKEN did not trigger copilot-review.yml.
Constraints: Only needed when a downstream workflow must react to the emitted event. A step whose effect has no downstream trigger can keep GITHUB_TOKEN.
applies: Applies to workflows in .github/workflows/ where one workflow's action must trigger another workflow; not to plain comments or labels that no workflow listens for.
says: Copilot marked its pull request ready for review, but automated code review never started.
Bot pull requests published out of draft status do not trigger automated review checks.
Why did the automated reviewer fail to launch when the bot published its pull request?
Ensure automated code reviews launch automatically after the bot marks its pull request ready.
